text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 28:
The relative speeds can be varied by changing the distance of the upper wheel from the center of the lower one. The one drives the other by the friction or adhesion, and this may be increased by facing the lower one with india-rubber.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 28; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_028.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 32:
Friction-wheels. The surfaces of these wheels are made rough, so as to bite as much as possible; one is sometimes faced with leather, or, better, with vulcanized india-rubber.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 32; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_032.html.

Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 204:
An illustration of the transmission of rotary motion from one shaft to another, arranged obliquely to it, by means of rolling contact.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 204; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_204.html.
